definitions.explanation: Forming an opinion or conclusion based on incomplete information or personal assumptions rather than evidence. Often carries a negative nuance, implying that the conclusion is unreliable.

examples.japanese: {憶測|おくそく}で{物|もの}を{言|い}うな。
examples.english: Don't say things based on speculation.

examples.japanese: {様々|さまざま}な{憶測|おくそく}が{飛|と}び{交|か}っている。
{事実|じじつ}を{確認|かくにん}せずに{憶測|おくそく}だけで{判断|はんだん}するのは{危険|きけん}だ。
examples.english: It's dangerous to make judgments based solely on speculation without confirming the facts.

notes:
USAGE:
{憶測|おくそく} generally has a negative connotation, implying that the conclusion drawn is not well-founded. It is common in news commentary and formal discussions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {憶測|おくそく}が{飛|と}び{交|か}う (speculation flies around)
- {憶測|おくそく}で{判断|はんだん}する (to judge based on speculation)
- {憶測|おくそく}に{過|す}ぎない (it's nothing more than speculation)
- {憶測|おくそく}を{呼|よ}ぶ (to invite speculation)
- {憶測|おくそく}{記事|きじ} (speculative article)

KANJI NOTE:
Also written as {臆測|おくそく} with a different first character. Both writings are accepted and have the same meaning.
